questions.prompt: What does the principle of least privilege require?

options.text: Every user and process gets only the access it needs — no more
Everyone gets administrator rights for convenience
Access is granted based on network location
Security depends on hiding the system's design

questions.explanation: Least privilege grants the minimum access needed, which limits the blast radius when an account is compromised.

questions.prompt: Relying on hidden design instead of real controls is called security through ____.
questions.explanation: Security through obscurity relies on secret designs or hidden URLs; open design (Kerckhoffs's principle) says security should rest on secret keys, not secret designs.

questions.prompt: Which are classic security design principles? Select all that apply.

options.text: Trust everything inside the network perimeter

questions.explanation: Fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, and separation of duties are core principles; trusting the internal perimeter is exactly what zero trust rejects.

questions.prompt: Match each principle to its meaning.

pairs.right: Deny by default when in doubt or on error
Never trust by location; verify every request

questions.explanation: Each principle turns into concrete controls: layered defenses, checking every access, denying by default, and verifying every request regardless of origin.

questions.prompt: Order these access states from most secure default to least secure, by the fail-safe principle.

items.text: Grant only what is explicitly needed

questions.explanation: Fail-safe defaults favor denying by default and granting the minimum; allowing everything and restricting later is the least secure posture.

questions.prompt: Why does 'psychological acceptability' matter as a security principle?

options.text: Controls that are too painful get bypassed, so usable security is what actually gets used
It makes obscurity a valid primary defense
It removes the need for authentication

questions.explanation: If security is too annoying people work around it, so effective controls must be usable — pairing strong controls with tools like password managers.
